The expanding width of the confidence intervals directly reflects the increasing uncertainty as we look further into the future. While the 90% confidence intervals capture a wide range of probable outcomes, specific high-impact risks or "black swan" events could push actual results outside these predicted ranges. Such events include sudden and severe economic shocks, like an unexpected recession or an unprecedented boom driven by a major technological breakthrough. Geopolitical crises, such as a rapid escalation of international conflicts or trade wars, could also trigger significant market reactions that are not easily modeled within standard forecasting frameworks. Similarly, unforeseen regulatory changes, a sudden shift in central bank monetary policy, or a major natural disaster impacting key industries could all create extreme deviations from typical patterns, leading to outcomes far beyond our current statistical expectations.
